title: Playing halls and his own bands; Wooden Joe at Moreau's
summary: He mostly led his own band and gave work to others; Wooden Joe, Lawrence Toca and Willie O'Connell played at Moreau's.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: How about some of the house halls you play in?

I play playing halls, I mean like that. Yeah. John Zami and all them halls, I play playing those halls. I play the halls, but you know, not regular jobs, you know what I mean? Yeah, special bands. Off jobs.
You usually had your own band then?

Oh yeah, I mostly worked by myself, mostly all the time. I had plenty of work at that time. I used to give work to every kid right there. Sometimes I had two, three jobs, I used to give them jobs on the side. Wooden Joe worked with me too a while. He worked with me on the last at Moreau. He was the last one worked with me at Moreau. Wooden Joe, Lawrence Morari, and Eddie Johnson. Eddie Johnson was a sacrifice. That was the last one when the place closed. They had added.

That was the last one worked with me after. Wooden Joe and Lawrence Morari. Sometimes he'd send Willie O'Connell in his place. I mean, in other words, he would work three nights a piece. One would work four nights, one a week, that one would make three nights.
Willie O'Connell is representative of the union in Beluxian, huh? Well, what does he play? Carlet? No, banjo.
One of your good banjo players.
Yeah, Willie O'Connell. He used to live with Lawrence, remember when he was living with Lawrence, I mean.
